artifact_reviews.summary: The revised public loop acquisition/borrowing rule preserves demonstrated synchronous extension compatibility. Cancellation-aware local monitoring has a concrete mechanism and precedence. Explicit cooperative-cleanup limitations and bounded test containment resolve the shutdown finding without a production lifecycle framework.

prior_findings.basis: An open non-running current loop is reused before factories/configure; ordinary clients borrow it without Runner ownership or unrelated cancellation. External server overrides preserve it, while base.start retains aiohttp's existing consume/close contract. Registration restoration and closed-loop handling are explicit. Separate raw-fresh and caller-loop tests prevent one from substituting for the other.
prior_findings.acceptance_remaining: Implement and execute actual revised client/server/edge entrypoints, success/error and post-configure ContextVars on both interpreters, including preconstructed resources and unrelated caller work.

prior_findings.basis: The done callback checks public Task.cancelling() after retrieving a completed exception, so cancellation converted into a finalizer error does not stop aiohttp's internal cleanup. Local cleanup disarms monitoring, avoids repeated cancellation, and preserves independent setup errors ahead of active failures and teardown diagnostics.
prior_findings.acceptance_remaining: Execute the mixed setup/finalizer/sibling case through the patched entrypoints, plus active periodic/edge failure and cleanup-only paths; replace only the specific loop-stopped error attributable to the monitor.

prior_findings.basis: The revision expressly states that Runner/aiohttp cancellation gathers and async-generator cleanup can stall, and that executor wait limits cannot kill threads. The harness owns 30+5+5 second bootstrap containment and 90+5+5 second round containment, records original-error/stage markers, terminates only owned processes and distinguishes forced containment from graceful completion or caller delivery.
prior_findings.acceptance_remaining: Implement stage-marked task/async-generator/executor stall variants and verify owned-process disappearance. Ordinary successful tests must return naturally. Hypothetical noncooperation is not a design blocker under the user's explicit scope.

artifact_reviews.complexity_assessment: Proportionate. Two F01 task handles, public current-loop registration and local cleanup variables suffice; the revised design removes the prior ContextVar sharing layer and excludes AppRunner replacement or a generic supervisor.
artifact_reviews.regression_assessment: No concrete new design regression found. Preserve synchronous dispatch, edge's absence of a periodic task, child-launch/seed ordering, existing os._exit and aiohttp ownership. A fresh 3.13 policy-created loop is deliberately treated as borrowed and released by the harness, not misreported as entrypoint-owned cleanup.
artifact_reviews.implementation_gate: Design PASS only. Phase 1A acceptance and actual startup/real-round regressions remain prerequisites.

artifact_reviews.summary: The supported-path scope now guards all aggregation dispatches before arithmetic, preserves the no-flag Metal/caller default, and defines borrowed host-array ownership. Resume remains a narrowly specified unselected proposal. Selected clipping/mode/device/RNG repairs and conditional optimization are proportionate.

prior_findings.basis: An owned baseline is captured before received-weight hooks. Every eligible raw tree is validated, including zero-weight trees; transformed effective trees and report/payload alignment are checked again before strategy aggregate_weights, legacy aggregate_weights or delta computation. Both arrival orders and malformed-last cases require failure before arithmetic/global load. The shared server integration has an explicit narrow 3A-after-2B handoff.
prior_findings.acceptance_remaining: Implement shared ingress and algorithm/trainer preflight together; demonstrate no partial mutation, hook-induced malformation rejection and valid independently trained 8/24 weighted results on all dispatches.

prior_findings.basis: No flags preserve mx.default_device() and caller stream choices, rather than Config.device()'s generic cpu fallback. Explicit cpu/mps flags retain CPU precedence. Factory initialization, numerical graph construction/execution and restoration receive exception-safe scopes. Prebuilt lazy-graph placement is expressly excluded from migration claims.
prior_findings.acceptance_remaining: Verify actual operation placement and restored caller defaults on no-flag/CPU/Metal/custom-stream success and failures; preserve mixed submodule modes and evaluation statistics.

prior_findings.basis: P4/E9 now define a committed step as a completed optimizer update with bookkeeping and an empty accumulation window. Mid-window checkpoint requests must defer or reject, never drop gradients or force early updates. A batch-independent accumulation oracle is separate from stochastic resume. Existing weight-only checkpoints retain their promise.
prior_findings.acceptance_remaining: No resume implementation is required for A1/A2. A separately selected future feature must pass E9, including mid-window requests and a committed partial tail.

prior_findings.basis: Extraction is documented as borrowed/read-only by contract. Retained baselines, delayed observations and malformed fixtures must recursively own copies; aggregation must not mutate borrowed inputs. Snapshot isolation is tested without promising universal extraction copies or adding hot-path copies without measurement.
prior_findings.acceptance_remaining: Apply snapshots at the specified consumers and verify baseline retention across training, with independent negative fixtures.

artifact_reviews.scope_assessment: A1/A2 and selected P1 are existing-path repairs. E8 is bounded qualification evidence; compile adoption requires reproducible benefit plus numerical/state/callback parity and remains default-eager. General resume, conversion, new models and broad scheduler/accumulation parity remain proposals. No blanket backend parity, new protocol, Torch-free packaging or lifecycle expansion is authorized.
artifact_reviews.regression_assessment: E5 protects the documented no-flag command and caller device/modes; E6 protects disabled clipping and rejects invalid/nonfinite clipping inputs; E7 uses stable logical client/round identities, covers reused workers and leaves existing selection/partition and unseeded semantics intact. No concrete new design regression found.
artifact_reviews.implementation_gate: Native Python 3.13 MLX profile still must be provisioned/accepted by its owner; absent MLX is not a passing required skip. E1-E8 and real transport qualification remain unexecuted here.

artifact_reviews.summary: Base and mandatory collection have practical concrete fixes and explicit prerequisites. Genuine optional native-tokenizer absence is distinct from mandatory Nanochat/DP omissions. Fixture restoration and the 59-location/60-message typing ledger are sound. Bounded CPU CI reuses the meaningful 1B runtime harness.

collection.basis: The candidate already separates test/dev groups and requires DP/MPC/RL/Nanochat for the full suite. A test-base group plus one profile switch is a small extension. Guarding absent Opacus before importing diff_privacy fixes the demonstrated base collection problem without swallowing arbitrary import errors. Base retains fake adapter/local MPC tests. Mandatory requires actual synthetic Nanochat trainer nodes and pinned source rather than accepting namespace discovery or missing-source skips.
collection.limits: No fresh base environment was installed and no pytest collection/suite was run. Candidate group changes, actual collection and prerequisite negatives remain implementation acceptance.

optional_skips.basis: The mandatory native tokenizer omission is capability-bound to callable rustbpe.Tokenizer, not find_spec alone. Missing/incompatible mandatory packages or synthetic source must fail. The base omissions name only the genuine optional DP module and real Nanochat integration nodes; fake optional-backend tests stay active.
optional_skips.complexity_guardrail: Keep the policy to the two fixed profiles, explicit prerequisites and qualification-run assertions. Use a small skip/xfail audit; do not build a configurable profile engine, discovery catalog or general reporting layer. Full-suite required-node assertions belong to the full qualification invocation, not ordinary focused developer runs or the separate runtime subset. The written design permits this narrow implementation, so there is no present overengineering blocker.

fixtures.basis: The baseline temp_config mutates shared Config state and redirects paths after construction. configure_environment restores env/argv before yield, discards prior params and lacks exception-safe post-yield restoration. Proposed snapshots, temporary-root arguments before construction, lifetime-correct env/argv and finally restoration address real defects. FedDF loader/Nanochat path scopes and Python/NumPy/CPU Torch RNG restoration are targeted; they do not require accelerator initialization or an event-loop fixture.
fixtures.acceptance_remaining: Nested contexts and setup/body exceptions must restore prior mutable values and registration, not merely reset the singleton. Reverse-order checks must preserve imports and helper functionality. F13 stays a production test within one fixture lifetime; fixture isolation cannot close it.

typing.assignment_coverage: All 59 live first-party (file,line,column,code) locations exactly match the design's assignments plus its referenced core triage entries; KNOT explicitly accounts for both messages.
typing.basis: The 38+11+10 breakdown is unique locations; the 60 emitted messages include 12 example messages. The design's historical-count caveat is accurate. Preserve nonzero ty output and scoped dispositions; intentional abstract-class negative tests retain their TypeError assertions and may use documented line-specific ignores.

ci.basis: A two-version ubuntu CPU matrix, separate locked base/mandatory environments, 25-minute job limit and finite provisioning/test steps replace unlocked all-extras and five unbounded download-heavy runs. ssl/llm_eval conflict in the candidate makes blanket all-extras unsuitable. Runtime tests retain real two-client parameter changes, actual socket/processor payloads, numerical weighting and owned-process containment. Python 3.14 is explicitly core forward evidence; robotics/MLX remain separately provisioned support checks.
ci.complexity_guardrail: Use the delivered 1B harness and ordinary pytest/JUnit/runner artifacts. Avoid a second subprocess supervisor, new timeout plugin or durable process-reporting subsystem. Use workflow timeouts as outer bounds; regular success still requires the harness's natural exit and no-survivor checks.
ci.acceptance_remaining: Coordinate runtime markers/paths with 1B and group/lock changes with 1A. Run actual Linux CPU jobs and retain counts, warnings and comparable coverage; the proposed deadlines are finite budgets, not measured Linux execution evidence.
